Strengthening with grain refinement has been traditionally rationalized on the basis of the so-called Hall-Petch mechanism.
Hence, the SMC alloy having both smaller grain size and higher dislocation density within the grain volume indicates higher strength compared to the MC alloy

The increase in volume fraction of grain boundary also leads to the predominance of the Coble creep, which is controlled by diffusion of vacancies along grain boundaries, over the Nabarro-Herring creep
Further increase in temperature to 350 /C14 C leads to a drastic softening of the SMC alloy, which is most probably associated with the operation of grain boundary sliding.
A drastic increase in total elongation as well as intense softening observed in the SMC alloy at the short-term test above 400 /C14 C indicates that superplastic deformation is likely to occur.
